metadata.proof: The review_document endpoint (PUT /api/documents/{doc_id}) only checks that the user is an underwriter or admin (line 174). It does NOT verify that the document belongs to an application assigned to that underwriter. An underwriter can approve, reject, or modify any document's status, review_notes, and rejection_reason by simply knowing the document's integer doc_id from the path parameter (line 168). The sink is at lines 185-191 where doc.status, doc.reviewer_id, doc.review_notes are mutated without ownership verification.

extra.message: Denial of Service — Unbounded Memory Consumption in CSV Borrower Import

metadata.proof: The import_borrowers endpoint (POST /api/admin/import/borrowers) reads the entire uploaded CSV file into memory as a single string on line 82 via `file.file.read()`. There is no file size limit — the only guard is the admin role check (line 79). A large multi-gigabyte CSV file will exhaust server memory. Additionally, the decoded string is wrapped in io.StringIO (line 83) and iterated with csv.DictReader, meaning both the raw bytes AND the decoded string representation coexist in memory simultaneously, doubling the memory footprint.

extra.message: Denial of Service — Unbounded Row Buffering in Export Applications Endpoint

metadata.proof: The export_applications endpoint (GET /api/admin/export/applications) loads ALL matching database records into memory via `q.all()` (line 151) without any LIMIT or pagination. Each row is then accumulated into a `rows` list (line 153) before being written to the CSV response. With thousands of applications, this could exhaust server memory. The admin-only role check (line 140) mitigates external attack surface but not accidental self-DoS or authorized-user DoS.

extra.message: Unbounded list_applications response can exhaust resources

metadata.proof: The GET /api/applications/ endpoint materializes the entire filtered query via .all() with no LIMIT, offset, or cursor pagination. For admin users (who bypass all row-level filters) or underwriters viewing the active queue, a large loan_application table causes excessive memory consumption on the DB driver and FastAPI server, and produces oversized JSON payloads that can lead to OOM or DoS.

extra.message: Unbounded list_documents response can exhaust resources

metadata.proof: The GET /api/documents/ endpoint calls .all() with no pagination. Underwriter, support_specialist, and admin roles can view all documents without row limits. Combined with the broad staff visibility (no per-application scoping for underwriter/support/admin), a single request can pull and serialize the entire documents table, causing memory exhaustion and slow responses.

extra.message: Unbounded list_users response can exhaust resources

metadata.proof: The GET /api/users/ endpoint (admin-only) returns the full user table via .all() with no pagination or limit. A large user base causes the entire users table to be loaded into memory and serialized in a single response, leading to high DB memory pressure, large JSON payloads, and potential worker timeouts or OOM.

extra.message: Unbounded CSV import can exhaust resources

metadata.proof: The POST /api/admin/import/borrowers endpoint reads the entire uploaded CSV into memory (file.file.read()), then iterates every row, creating a DB user + BorrowerProfile and committing per row. A malicious or oversized CSV causes OOM on the server, fills disk with temp data, and floods the database with individual INSERT+COMMIT operations, enabling a resource-exhaustion DoS.

extra.message: Unbounded applications export can exhaust memory

metadata.proof: The GET /api/admin/export/applications endpoint loads every matching LoanApplication row into memory via q.all(), then builds a second in-memory rows list and serializes to CSV/JSON. No server-side cursor, streaming, or pagination is used. A large applications table can crash the worker with OOM or cause request timeouts.

extra.message: Unbounded decisions export can exhaust memory
